title: Policy
description: Three mutability classes. 'constitutional' = principal-only. 'operational' = agent-mutable within constitutional ceilings. 'frozen' (v0.2.0) = amendable by nobody, bound to one Claim, issued inside that Claim's pre-registration window. See policy.md.

class.description: Meta-constitutional: this classification is itself constitutional and cannot be changed by agents. The class axis is amendment AUTHORITY: constitutional = principal only; operational = agent, within constitutional ceilings; frozen = nobody, including the principal (supersession is via a successor Claim, not amendment).

field_path.description: Dotted path of the governed setting, e.g. 'capital.max_at_risk' or 'exploration.weight'.

value.description: The setting value. Type is domain-determined.

version.description: Monotonic version of this Policy id's amendment chain. Required so that decisions can unambiguously cite resolved-at-decision-time version and rollback can restore by version.

amendment_authority.description: Who may amend. MUST be non-empty for constitutional and operational (re-imposed in allOf). MUST be the empty array for frozen — 'nobody may amend this' is the whole point of the class, and it must be WRITABLE. In v0.1.0 this field was minItems:1, which made an unamendable policy unexpressible; that is the gap ADR-0041 hit.

ratification_rule.description: kind='none' is legal ONLY for class=frozen, where there is no amendment to ratify. Conversely frozen MUST use 'none': an 'evidence_threshold' ratification on a frozen gate would be a gate re-openable by evidence, which is the thing the class exists to forbid. additionalProperties:false so an undeclared field cannot smuggle in ratification mechanics a validator will ignore but a naive adapter might honor.

condition.description: Expressed as a canon-query predicate. Interpreted by runtime; canon records verbatim.

restore_version.description: Target version to restore (default: immediate predecessor).

precedence.description: Ordered rule ids; lower index wins when multiple fire concurrently. Validators MUST verify this is a permutation of rules[*].id (see canon.md 'Validator-level rules').

provenance.description: Ordered chain of prior versions. First entry is genesis.

effective_until.description: Null means open-ended. MUST be null for class=frozen: a frozen policy is bounded by CLAIM SCOPE, not by time. Its horizon is the life of the Claim it is bound to, which is not a timestamp knowable at emission.

bound_to_claim_id.description: REQUIRED for class=frozen, FORBIDDEN otherwise. The Claim whose pre-registration this policy is part of. This is what makes the policy eval-local rather than framework-level: it may be cited only by Decisions that arbitrate over this Claim (validator rule 12), and it is superseded only when the Claim is (via Decision.successor_claim_id), never by amendment.

derived_from.description: OPTIONAL, and legal only for class=frozen. An RFC-6901 JSON Pointer into the bound Claim envelope (e.g. '/thresholds'). When present, validators MUST check that Policy.value is canonical-JSON-equal to the Claim subtree at this pointer (validator rule 14). This is how a frozen Policy proves it carries ZERO information not already hash-bound in the immutable Claim — it is a VIEW of the pre-registration, not a restatement of it, and therefore adds no degrees of freedom. Omit it only when the governed value genuinely does not appear in the Claim.

allOf.description: class=frozen: amendable by nobody, bound to exactly one Claim, single genesis version, no rollback, no ratification, no expiry timestamp. Every degree of freedom that ADR-0041's review identified as still-discretionary under a hand-constrained 'operational' policy (ratification_rule, rollback_rule, amendment_authority, provenance) is closed HERE, by the class, mechanically.

ratification_rule.description: Exactly {kind: 'none'} and nothing else. A stray required_evidence_count alongside kind='none' is inert to a correct validator but reads as ratification machinery to a careless one.

scope.description: A frozen Policy MUST NOT be framework-scoped. It is bound to one Claim, and Claims live at a layer/instance — a framework-scoped frozen Policy is a category error, and worse, it is the shape a self-authorization land-grab would take (a framework 'ceiling' an agent minted for itself that nobody, including the principal, can amend). Also excludes 'layer:L<n>' role-profile scope.

allOf.description: constitutional and operational: unchanged from v0.1.0. amendment_authority stays non-empty; the frozen-only fields are forbidden; ratification kind 'none' is forbidden (a mutable policy with nothing to ratify an amendment against is an unguarded policy).
